## Part 1: Fun with Functions

```{r}
#check wd
library(here)

#load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytuesdayR)

#Part 1A: Exponential Transformation

Exp <- function(x, k) {
  fun1A <- 1  #first term
  for (i in 1:k) {        #create for loop
    fun1A <- fun1A + (x^i) / factorial(i)
  }
  
  return(fun1A)
}

# Example output
print(Exp(2, 7))


```

```{r}
#Part 1B: Sample mean and sample sd

# Function to calculate the sample mean
sample_mean <- function(x) {
  N <- length(x)  # Get the number of observations
  sum_x <- 0  # Initialize the sum
  for (i in 1:N) {
    sum_x <- sum_x + x[i]  # Add each element to the sum
  }
  return(sum_x / N)  # Return the average
}

# Function to calculate the sample standard deviation
sample_sd <- function(x) {
  N <- length(x)  # Get the number of observations
  mean_x <- sample_mean(x)  # Compute the sample mean
  
  sum_squared_diff <- 0  # Initialize the sum of squared differences
  for (i in 1:N) {
    sum_squared_diff <- sum_squared_diff + (x[i] - mean_x)^2  # Compute the squared differences
  }
  
  return(sqrt(sum_squared_diff / (N - 1)))  # Return the sample standard deviation
}

# Example output:

sample_mean(c(12, 25, 13, 42, 67))  
sample_sd(c(12, 25, 13, 42, 67))  

```

```{r}
# Part 1C: Confidence Intervals
# Assuming sample_mean and sample_sd functions already exist

calculate_CI <- function(x, conf = 0.95) {
  N <- length(x)  # Get the number of observations
  mean_x <- sample_mean(x)  # sample mean
  sd_x <- sample_sd(x)  # sample sd
  SE <- sd_x / sqrt(N)  # Standard error of the mean
  
  alpha <- 1 - conf  # alpha
  degrees_freedom <- N - 1  # Df for the t-distribution
  t_score <- qt(p = alpha / 2, df = degrees_freedom, lower.tail = FALSE)  # t-score
  
  # confidence interval
  margin_of_error <- t_score * SE
  lower_bound <- mean_x - margin_of_error
  upper_bound <- mean_x + margin_of_error
  
  # Return the confidence interval as a named vector
  return(c(lower_bound = lower_bound, upper_bound = upper_bound))
}

# Example output:

# 95% confidence interval
calculate_CI(c(12, 25, 13, 42, 67),conf = 0.95)

# 99% confidence interval
calculate_CI(c(12, 25, 13, 42, 67),conf = 0.99)

#Check func. matches existing func. in R

dat <- data.frame(x = c(12, 25, 13, 42, 67))
fit <- lm(x ~ 1, dat)

# Calculate a 95% confidence interval
confint(fit, level = 0.95)

```

## Part 2: Wrangling Data

```{r}
#Manually create a data subdirectory
#check to see if files already exist with if()
#next download data from tidytuesday and save to data subdirectory
library(here)
if (!file.exists(here("data", "tuesdata_rainfall.RDS"))) {
    tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load("2020-01-07")
    rainfall <- tuesdata$rainfall
    temperature <- tuesdata$temperature

    # save the files to RDS objects
    saveRDS(tuesdata$rainfall, file = here("data", "tuesdata_rainfall.RDS"))
    saveRDS(tuesdata$temperature, file = here("data", "tuesdata_temperature.RDS"))
}

#Load datasets
rainfall <- readRDS(here("data", "tuesdata_rainfall.RDS"))
temperature <- readRDS(here("data", "tuesdata_temperature.RDS"))

#take a glimpse at the data
library(tidyverse)

glimpse(rainfall)
glimpse(temperature)
```

```{r}
#Load Libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(lubridate)

#drop rows with NAs in rainfall

rainfall_na_gone <- rainfall %>% drop_na()

#create new date column (year+month+day)
#create new column with year only

rainfall_na_gone <- rainfall_na_gone %>%
  mutate(
    date = ymd(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-")), 
    year_only = year(date)  
)

#convert city_name to uppercase
rainfall_na_gone <- rainfall_na_gone %>%
  mutate(city_name = str_to_upper(city_name))

#join rainfall and temp datasets using innerjoin
#to keep only obs present in both datasets

df <- rainfall_na_gone %>%
  inner_join(temperature, by = c("date" = "date", "city_name" = "city_name"))

#print results of join
as_tibble(df)

```

##Part 3: Data visualization

```{r}
# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Step 1: Filter data for years 2014 and onwards
df_filt <- df %>%
  filter(year >= 2014)

###having a hard time changing color for max and min here##

# Step 2: Create the plot
ggplot( data = df_filt, mapping =  aes(x = date, y = temperature)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = temp_type)) +
    facet_wrap(~ city_name, scales = "free_y") +  # Facet by city_name
    scale_color_manual(values = c("min" = "blue", "max" = "red")) + 
    labs(
    title = "Max and Min Temperatures Over Time (2014 and onwards)",
    subtitle = "Trends in maximum and minimum temperatures for each city",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Temperature (°C)",
    color = "Temp type",
    caption = "Data source: df dataset from Part 2"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +  # Use a minimal theme
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

ggplot( data = df_after_2014, mapping = aes(x = date, y = temperature)) +
```
